subject: FinBank — DR mutual action plan + technical follow-ups (Redwood Private)
body:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@finbank.com>, James O'Connor <james.oconnor@finbank.com>
Cc: FinBank DR Program <dr-program@finbank.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 3:07 PM
Subject: FinBank — DR mutual action plan + technical follow-ups (Redwood Private)

Sarah, James —

Thanks again for the time today. Below is a proposed mutual action plan to validate Redwood Private DR/backup readiness against FinBank’s requirements. I also dropped links to the current draft runbooks so your infra/SRE folks can start reviewing.

Mutual action plan (draft)
1) FinBank → Redwood: share current target architecture + constraints
   - Kubernetes distro (EKS vs self-managed), version target
   - Single-region vs cross-region DR intent (active/passive?)
   - Storage backends allowed for backups (S3, NFS, etc.) + any egress restrictions
   - Key management requirements (AWS KMS, CloudHSM, customer-managed keys)
   - RPO/RTO targets by component (control plane config DB, object store, audit logs)

2) Redwood → FinBank: confirm support posture + recommended patterns
   - What Redwood backs up (control-plane state, config, routing policy, etc.) vs what’s intentionally out-of-scope
   - Reference runbooks (backup, restore, DR in-region)
   - Validation approach (smoke tests + restore drill)

3) Joint: DR validation session (90 mins)
   - Walkthrough of backup/restore flow
   - Review restore ordering + rollback criteria
   - Identify any gaps for FinBank compliance evidence

Draft runbook links (internal docs, OK to share for review; still marked “Draft”)
- Overview: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/Private+Day-2+Ops%3A+Backup+%26+Restore+Overview
- Control-plane backup (draft): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/Runbook%3A+Control+Plane+Backup+(Draft)
- Control-plane restore (draft): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/Runbook%3A+Control+Plane+Restore+(Draft)
- DR plan (VPC single-region draft): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/DR+Plan%3A+VPC+Single-Region+(Draft)

Attachment: Redwood_Private_DR_Validation_Checklist_v0.3.pdf

To unblock the next step, could you send:
- A high-level diagram (even 1 slide is fine) showing VPC layout, subnets/AZs, and where you’d like backups to land.
- Your current “must hit” RPO/RTO numbers (even if provisional) and which components they apply to.

If helpful, I can also pull in our product owner for Private deployments for the next call.

Best,
Markus

—
Markus Klein
Solutions Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference
markus@redwoodinference.com



From: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@finbank.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: James O'Connor <james.oconnor@finbank.com>, FinBank DR Program <dr-program@finbank.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 8:41 AM
Subject: Re: FinBank — DR mutual action plan + technical follow-ups (Redwood Private)

Markus —

Thanks. This is helpful.

Attaching a high-level architecture slide deck (sanitized). We’re leaning EKS (1.29) in a single AWS region initially, multi-AZ, with a longer-term goal of cross-region restore (not active/active).

Initial targets (still being finalized):
- Control plane config/state: RPO 15 min, RTO 2 hours
- Audit logs: RPO 60 min, RTO 24 hours (we prioritize retention/export evidence over fast restore)

Constraints:
- Backups must be encrypted with customer-managed keys (AWS KMS), and we need clarity on how key rotation is handled.
- We prefer S3 for backup artifacts; NFS is possible but not preferred.
- Outbound egress from the cluster is restricted; we can allow S3 endpoints/VPC gateway endpoints.

Questions on the draft docs:
1) Does restore assume a clean cluster, or can it target an existing cluster (post-incident) if namespaces are intact?
2) Do you back up “Kubernetes objects” (CRDs/Helm release state) or just Redwood control-plane state?

Attachment: FinBank_RedwoodPrivate_HighLevel_Architecture_v1.pptx

Sarah Patel
Director, Resilience Engineering
FinBank



From: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@finbank.com>
Cc: James O'Connor <james.oconnor@finbank.com>, FinBank DR Program <dr-program@finbank.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 10:12 AM
Subject: Re: FinBank — DR mutual action plan + technical follow-ups (Redwood Private)

Sarah —

Perfect, thank you for the deck + the targets. I’ve looped in Vivek (Product, Private Deployments) so we can be crisp on what we support and what we recommend for your RPO/RTO.

Quick answers (more detail below):
1) Restore target: our recommended/validated path is restore into a clean cluster. We can talk through “restore into existing” as a best-effort path, but we typically treat that as higher risk (stale CRDs, partial Helm state, lingering controllers).
2) Backup scope: Redwood’s toolkit focuses on Redwood control-plane state + deterministic config capture (Helm values/manifests) needed to redeploy. We do NOT treat “Kubernetes cluster backup” (etcd restore) as the primary mechanism, but we provide guidance on when to use it.

Details:
- Clean cluster restore is what our DR plan is built around: bootstrap cluster → install Redwood Private → apply restore artifact → run validation. This avoids hidden state in k8s.
- For Kubernetes objects: we capture the Redwood deployment configuration (Helm values + select manifests) as part of the backup manifest so redeploy is deterministic. We do not rely solely on backing up etcd or snapshotting all namespaces.
- On encryption/rotation: backup artifacts are encrypted at rest; with AWS KMS we support CMKs (customer-managed keys). We can walk through envelope encryption + rotation expectations and what happens if KMS is temporarily unavailable.

If you’re open to it, next step would be a 60–90 minute technical validation working session:
- Review your architecture constraints (restricted egress + VPC endpoints)
- Map to our reference patterns (S3+KMS, least-privilege IAM)
- Align on DR drill plan + what “evidence artifacts” we can provide (logs, manifests, checksum verification)

Proposed times (ET):
- Mon 2/17 1:00–2:30pm
- Tue 2/18 10:00–11:30am

Vivek — anything you want to add re: cross-region restore posture (near-term vs roadmap) before they commit assumptions?

Best,
Markus



From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@finbank.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>, James O'Connor <james.oconnor@finbank.com>, FinBank DR Program <dr-program@finbank.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: FinBank — DR mutual action plan + technical follow-ups (Redwood Private)

Sarah, James —

Jumping in (I’m the PM for Redwood Private deployments). Thanks for the clarity on targets/constraints.

On cross-region restore: we support and document single-region DR (restore into a clean cluster in-region) as the baseline. For cross-region, the key dependency is ensuring backups are replicated and keys are usable in the target region (KMS policy + replication strategy). We can support a cross-region restore runbook as a guided pattern (i.e., “restore into a clean cluster in a new region using replicated artifacts”), but we’ll want to confirm assumptions around DNS/TLS and any region-specific endpoints.

On KMS/encryption posture: our direction is envelope encryption with a customer-managed CMK where applicable, with deterministic restore and explicit failure modes if KMS is unavailable.

Happy to join the technical validation session. Tue 2/18 10:00–11:30am ET works for me.

Regards,
Vivek

Thanks both.

Two additional items we need to close before we can sign off internally:
1) DNS/TLS during restore: We terminate via ACM + internal ALB. During DR restore into a clean cluster, do you recommend reusing certs/DNS names, or staging under a new hostname and cutover?
2) KMS dependency: If AWS KMS has an outage (regional), what is the expected behavior of backup jobs and restores? (We want to make sure we don’t create an RTO risk by requiring KMS at restore time without a fallback.)

Tue 2/18 10:00–11:30am ET works.

Principal Platform Engineer

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
To: James O'Connor <james.oconnor@finbank.com>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@finbank.com>, FinBank DR Program <dr-program@finbank.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 11:32 AM
Subject: Re: FinBank — DR mutual action plan + technical follow-ups (Redwood Private)

James —

Great questions; these are exactly the “practical DR” details we want to validate with you.

1) DNS/TLS approach
- Recommended: stage restore under a temporary hostname (e.g., private-dr-restore.<domain>) to run validations, then cut over DNS once the restore validation passes.
- If you must reuse the same hostname, it’s possible but we treat it as higher-risk because it can complicate rollback if validation fails.
- For ACM/internal ALB: we typically see customers pre-provision the ALB + cert association as part of the “bootstrap” step, then point services after restore.

2) KMS dependency / outage behavior
- Backup creation: if KMS is unavailable, encryption will fail closed (backup job fails) rather than writing unencrypted artifacts.
- Restore: the restore needs to decrypt the artifact; if KMS is unavailable at restore time, restore will not proceed.
- The mitigation pattern we’ll walk through: ensure DR runbooks include KMS availability considerations, and (for cross-region) key policy/replication so the target region can decrypt.

We’ll bring a concrete “expected failure modes” section to the session and map it to your RTO assumptions.

Calendar invite for Tue 2/18 10:00–11:30am ET coming separately.

Best,
Markus
